name: Tracheal Anomaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Tracheal Anomalies

criteria.description: Presence of congenital narrowing or malformation of the tracheal lumen confirmed by imaging
Clinical signs of respiratory distress such as stridor or recurrent respiratory infections
Visualization of tracheal anomaly by bronchoscopy
Presence of associated congenital cardiac anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of airway narrowing confirmed by imaging or bronchoscopy plus clinical respiratory symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including pulmonology and otolaryngology

searchTerms: blue skin during feeding or crying
turning purple when eating or upset

occasional.symptomName: Stridor exacerbated by upper respiratory infections
Failure to thrive due to feeding difficulties
searchTerms: poor growth due to feeding problems
failure to gain weight from eating difficulties

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary hypertension secondary to chronic hypoxia
searchTerms: lung artery hypertension from low oxygen
pulmonary hypertension due to chronic hypoxia

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible hypoxemia on arterial blood gas during respiratory distress
imaging: CT scan or MRI showing tracheal narrowing or malformation
Bronchoscopy revealing structural anomalies of the trachea
Chest X-ray may show airway narrowing or associated lung changes
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; may be associated with syndromic conditions
other: Pulmonary function tests showing obstructive airway pattern
Echocardiography to assess for associated cardiac anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: Supraglottic airway collapse rather than tracheal narrowing
External compression of trachea by vascular structures
Identified by imaging showing vascular anomaly
Dynamic collapse of tracheal walls during expiration

redFlags: Failure to thrive due to feeding difficulties
references: Kuo, C. L., et al. (2019). Congenital tracheal anomalies: diagnosis and management. Pediatric Respiratory Reviews.
Fitzgerald, D. A., & Fitzgerald, D. A. (2017). Congenital tracheal stenosis and tracheomalacia. Paediatric Respiratory Reviews.
